name: Question 11
problem: Let $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -7\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2}},$ where ${c}_{1}=4{b}_{1}+{b}_{2}$ and ${c}_{2}=2{b}_{1}?$
worked_solution:
We are given that

$$
{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}=4{b}_{1}+{b}_{2} \\ {c}_{2}=2{b}_{1}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we express the $b$'s in terms of $c$'s. From the second equation, we get 

$$
{b}_{1}=\frac{1}{2}{c}_{2}.
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{c}_{1}=4(\frac{1}{2}{c}_{2})+{b}_{2}\,⟹\,{b}_{2}={c}_{1}-2{c}_{2}.
$$

Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -7\end{aligned}]$, we can write the vector $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={b}_{1}-7{b}_{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{c}_{2}-7({c}_{1}-2{c}_{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{c}_{2}-7{c}_{1}+14{c}_{2} \\  & =-7{c}_{1}+\frac{29}{2}{c}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ \frac{29}{2}\end{aligned}].$

Question 11
?

Let B={b1,b2} be a basis of R2 and [x]B=[1−7]. What are the coordinates of x relative to the basis C={c1,c2}, where c1=4b1+b2 and c2=2b1?

a
[x]C=[−729]
b
[x]C=[72]
c
[x]C=[292−7]
d
[x]C=[−7292]
e
[x]C=[7292]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We are given that

{c1=4b1+b2c2=2b1.

First, we express the b's in terms of c's. From the second equation, we get

b1=12c2.

Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

c1=4(12c2)+b2⟹b2=c1−2c2.

Since [x]B=[1−7], we can write the vector x as follows:

x=b1−7b2=12c2−7(c1−2c2)=12c2−7c1+14c2=−7c1+292c1

Therefore, [x]C=[−7292].
